title: DNA triangular prism-engineered multicolor chemiluminescence capsules for multiplexed visual detection of nucleic acid biomarkers.
abstract: Chemiluminescence (CL) capsules, featuring long-lasting emission and facile functionalization, hold great potential for multiplexed analysis of nucleic acid biomarkers. Herein, we report a strategy that utilizes DNA triangular prism (TP) scaffolds to spatially engineer trivalent catalytic hairpin assembly (CHA) amplification on multicolor CL capsules for the multiplexed visual detection of avian influenza virus (AIV) DNA biomarkers. Three multicolor CL capsules are fabricated by co-encapsulating luminol alone, luminol with coumarin 6 (C6), and luminol with both C6 and Nile red (NR), denoted as LUM@TP-3H2, C6/LUM@TP-3H4, and NR/C6/LUM@TP-3H6. TP-3DNAzyme exhibits approximately 1.6-fold higher peroxidase-like activity than free DNAzyme in solution, and TP-functionalized capsules show stronger CL signals and higher CL amplification efficiency than capsules with directly anchored CHA hairpins. Upon target-triggered CHA reaction and H2O2 addition, these TP-functionalized capsules generate blue, green, and red light, respectively, through chemiluminescence resonance energy transfer (CRET), along with an intense and long-lasting CL emission over 1200 s. The capsule-based CL imaging assay is recorded with a common smartphone, exhibiting a linear range of 10-1000 pM and detection limits of 0.57 pM, 0.82 pM, and 1.97 pM for H1N1, H5N1, and H7N9, respectively, with recoveries of 97.41-104.87% in 100-fold diluted human serum. Altogether, this work provides a versatile CRET platform by using TP-engineered multicolor capsules with trivalent CHA amplification for smartphone-based multiplexed visual detection.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to develop a novel method for the multiplexed visual detection of nucleic acid biomarkers, particularly for avian influenza virus (AIV) DNA, leveraging the unique properties of chemiluminescence (CL) capsules and DNA triangular prism (TP) scaffolds.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved the fabrication of three multicolor CL capsules using DNA triangular prism scaffolds and tested their performance for the detection of AIV DNA biomarkers, including specific subtypes such as H5N1 and H7N9.
analysis.methods: The researchers designed a CL imaging assay using TP-engineered multicolor capsules with trivalent catalytic hairpin assembly (CHA) amplification, where CL signals were generated through chemiluminescence resonance energy transfer (CRET) upon target-triggered reactions.
analysis.main_results: TP-functionalized capsules demonstrated stronger CL signals and higher amplification efficiency compared to capsules with directly anchored CHA hairpins, with detection limits of 0.57 pM, 0.82 pM, and 1.97 pM for H1N1, H5N1, and H7N9, respectively.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that the TP-engineered multicolor CL capsules offer a versatile platform for smartphone-based multiplexed visual detection of AIV DNA biomarkers, enhancing the sensitivity and specificity of diagnostic methods.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This method could improve the surveillance and diagnosis of avian influenza A viruses, particularly in resource-limited settings, by enabling rapid, visual, and sensitive detection of multiple viral subtypes using a smartphone.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to abstract-level reporting, and the evidence strength is moderate due to the lack of detailed experimental data and validation in real-world clinical or field settings.

analysis.summary_en: This study introduces a novel method for the multiplexed visual detection of avian influenza virus (AIV) DNA biomarkers using DNA triangular prism (TP)-engineered multicolor chemiluminescence (CL) capsules. The researchers fabricated three CL capsules with varying compositions and tested their performance for detecting specific AIV subtypes, including H5N1 and H7N9. The TP-functionalized capsules showed enhanced CL signals and amplification efficiency compared to traditional methods. The results indicate that this platform could offer a sensitive and versatile tool for AIV detection, particularly in low-resource environments. However, the study is based solely on abstract-level reporting, which limits the confidence in the findings. The method leverages chemiluminescence resonance energy transfer (CRET) and trivalent catalytic hairpin assembly (CHA) to generate distinct colors for different viral subtypes, enabling visual identification without complex instrumentation. The study highlights the potential of this approach for improving surveillance and diagnosis of AIV, but further validation in real-world settings is needed.

title_zh: DNA 三棱柱设计的多色化学发光胶囊,用于核酸生物标志物的多重视觉检测。

abstract_zh: 化学发光(CL)胶囊具有持久发射和易于功能化的特点,在核酸生物标志物的多重分析中具有巨大的潜力。在此,我们报告了一种利用 DNA 三棱柱 (TP) 支架在多色 CL 胶囊上空间设计三价催化发夹组装 (CHA) 扩增的策略,用于 禽流感 病毒 (AIV) DNA 生物标志物的多重视觉检测。通过单独共封装鲁米诺、鲁米诺与香豆素 6 (C6)、鲁米诺与 C6 和尼罗红 (NR) 共封装,制备了三种多色 CL 胶囊,分别表示为 LUM@TP-3H2、C6/LUM@TP-3H4 和 NR/C6/LUM@TP-3H6。TP-3DNAzyme 的过氧化物酶样活性比溶液中的游离 DNAzyme 高约 1.6 倍,并且 TP 功能化胶囊比直接锚定 CHA 发夹的胶囊显示出更强的 CL 信号和更高的 CL 扩增效率。在目标触发 CHA 反应和添加 H2O2 后,这些 TP 功能化胶囊通过化学发光共振能量转移 (CRET) 分别产生蓝光、绿光和红光,并发出超过 1200 秒的强烈而持久的 CL 发射。基于胶囊的 CL 成像测定是用普通智能手机记录的,对 H1N1、H5N1 和 H7N9 的线性范围为 10-1000 pM,检测限分别为 0.57 pM、0.82 pM 和 1.97 pM,在 100 倍稀释的人血清中回收率为 97.41-104.87%。总而言之,这项工作通过使用 TP 设计的多色胶囊和三价 CHA 扩增,为基于智能手机的多重视觉检测提供了一个多功能的 CRET 平台。

title: Awareness, attitude and adoption of avian influenza biosecurity practices among smallholder poultry farmers
abstract: Avian influenza remains an important threat to poultry production and farmers’ livelihoods, particularly in smallholder systems where biosecurity practices are often limited. The present study assessed farmers’ awareness, attitude and adoption of recommended avian influenza biosecurity practices and examined their association with selected socioeconomic characteristics. The study was conducted during 2019-20 in 14 villages covering all seven blocks of Jabalpur district, Madhya Pradesh. A total of 140 smallholder poultry farmers keeping fewer than 100 birds were selected through multistage sampling and interviewed using structured schedules. Awareness was assessed using a 25-item schedule, attitude using an adopted 14-item scale, and adoption using a 43-item schedule covering five biosecurity domains. Data were analyzed using frequency, percentage, correlation and multiple regression. The findings showed that 60.71% of farmers had low awareness, while only 12.86% had high awareness. Very low attitude scores were observed among 54.29% of farmers. Overall, most farmers (82.86%) had very low adoption of the recommended biosecurity practices, while only 1.42% showed a high level of adoption. Awareness and attitude were positively associated with adoption. The findings highlight the need for practical training, accessible veterinary extension services and locally relevant communication to help farmers improve biosecurity practices at the farm level.
journal: International Journal of Agriculture Extension and Social Development

title: The Psychological Impacts of Avian Influenza
abstract: Psychological factors have been neglected in preparation guidelines for an avian influenza (AVI) pandemic. To address this gap, a narrative literature review was conducted to (1) examine how AVI outbreaks—so far largely contained to livestock—have psychologically impacted people, and (2) consider the implications if an AVI pandemic were to emerge, in which large numbers of people would be infected. Findings indicate that AVI outbreaks have been characterized by fear, disgust, and avoidance of poultry products. Many of the other psychological phenomena observed in AVI outbreaks have been documented in past pandemics and other infectious outbreaks: Blame and anger, disease-related avoidance and stigmatization, xenophobia, conspiracy theories, panic buying, and personal stockpiling have all arisen in response to AVI outbreaks. These psychological phenomena may persist and intensify if AVI outbreaks evolve into a pandemic. The lessons learned from COVID-19 can be used to prepare for a possible AVI pandemic. However, additional measures may be needed. Fear, disgust, and avoidance of specific foods would likely distinguish an AVI pandemic from COVID-19. The threat of infected food triggers disgust, and so food-related disgust would likely be a prominent emotional reaction during an AVI pandemic. Public messaging from health authorities and others has the potential to either ease or exacerbate public concerns about food safety, depending on how the messages are crafted.

title: Probiotics as a Strategy for Mitigating Viral Infections in Poultry: Immunomodulatory Mechanisms and Therapeutic Potential.
abstract: Poultry viral infections remain a persistent challenge for the poultry industry, causing significant economic losses and posing potential threats to human health. The escalating frequency of outbreaks involving pathogens, such as infectious bronchitis virus (IBV), Newcastle disease virus (NDV) and avian influenza virus (AIV), underscores the urgent need for effective interventions. Probiotics have gained attention as a promising strategy to combat these viral infections due to their potential in enhancing immune responses and establishing a healthy gut microbiome. A literature search was carried out on Google Scholar, Scopus and PubMed using key search terms, such as 'probiotics', 'Lactobacillus', 'acidophilus', 'poultry', 'viral infections', 'Newcastle Disease Virus (NDV)' and other relevant terms. Inclusion criteria for manuscripts used were based on the relevance to probiotic-based interventions in poultry, the focus on immunological mechanisms and the examination of viral pathogens commonly found in West African poultry farming systems. This review explores the role of probiotics in mitigating the effects of NDV, AIV and IBV in poultry, focusing on their immunomodulatory effects and antiviral mechanisms. Lactobacillus acidophilus, L. plantarum have shown an interesting promise in countering NDV infections by modulating immunological parameters and enhancing antibody responses. Similarly, these probiotics have exhibited antiviral activity against AIV, promoting immune activation and reducing viral loads. plantarum have emerged as potential adjuvants for IBV vaccines, improving antibody responses and humoural immunity.

title_original: Probiotics as a Strategy for Mitigating Viral Infections in Poultry: Immunomodulatory Mechanisms and Therapeutic Potential.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the use of probiotics to mitigate viral infections in poultry, particularly avian influenza A viruses, by examining their immunomodulatory effects and antiviral mechanisms. The central question is whether probiotics can serve as an effective strategy for reducing the impact of these viruses on poultry health and potentially human health through zoonotic transmission.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review conducted a literature search on Google Scholar, Scopus, and PubMed using terms like 'probiotics', 'Lactobacillus', 'acidophilus', 'poultry', 'viral infections', 'Newcastle Disease Virus (NDV)', and other relevant terms. Inclusion criteria were based on the relevance to probiotic-based interventions in poultry, the focus on immunological mechanisms, and the examination of viral pathogens common in West African poultry farming systems.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Probiotics, particularly Lactobacillus acidophilus and Lactobacillus plantarum, have shown potential in modulating immunological parameters, enhancing antibody responses, and reducing viral loads against avian influenza A viruses (AIV). These findings suggest that probiotics may be a viable strategy for improving immune defenses against AIV in poultry.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review highlights the need for more targeted studies on probiotics' effects against specific avian influenza subtypes, such as H5N1 and H5N6. There is limited evidence on the long-term efficacy of probiotics in preventing zoonotic transmission of AIV to humans, and further research is required to address these gaps.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Future research should prioritize investigating the efficacy of probiotics against specific avian influenza subtypes and their role in preventing zoonotic transmission. Practical applications may include integrating probiotics into poultry farming practices to enhance immune responses and reduce the economic and public health burden of AIV outbreaks.

analysis.summary_en: This review evaluates the potential of probiotics, particularly Lactobacillus acidophilus and Lactobacillus plantarum, in mitigating avian influenza A virus (AIV) infections in poultry. It highlights their immunomodulatory effects and antiviral properties, suggesting they may enhance immune defenses and reduce viral loads. However, the review identifies gaps in understanding the long-term efficacy of probiotics against specific AIV subtypes and their role in zoonotic transmission. The findings support further research into targeted probiotic interventions and their integration into poultry farming practices to improve health outcomes and reduce economic losses associated with AIV outbreaks.

elements_en.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the use of probiotics to mitigate viral infections in poultry, particularly avian influenza A viruses, by examining their immunomodulatory effects and antiviral mechanisms. The central question is whether probiotics can serve as an effective strategy for reducing the impact of these viruses on poultry health and potentially human health through zoonotic transmission.
elements_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review conducted a literature search on Google Scholar, Scopus, and PubMed using terms like 'probiotics', 'Lactobacillus', 'acidophilus', 'poultry', 'viral infections', 'Newcastle Disease Virus (NDV)', and other relevant terms. Inclusion criteria were based on the relevance to probiotic-based interventions in poultry, the focus on immunological mechanisms, and the examination of viral pathogens common in West African poultry farming systems.
elements_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Probiotics, particularly Lactobacillus acidophilus and Lactobacillus plantarum, have shown potential in modulating immunological parameters, enhancing antibody responses, and reducing viral loads against avian influenza A viruses (AIV). These findings suggest that probiotics may be a viable strategy for improving immune defenses against AIV in poultry.
elements_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review highlights the need for more targeted studies on probiotics' effects against specific avian influenza subtypes, such as H5N1 and H5N6. There is limited evidence on the long-term efficacy of probiotics in preventing zoonotic transmission of AIV to humans, and further research is required to address these gaps.
elements_en.research_and_practice_implications: Future research should prioritize investigating the efficacy of probiotics against specific avian influenza subtypes and their role in preventing zoonotic transmission. Practical applications may include integrating probiotics into poultry farming practices to enhance immune responses and reduce the economic and public health burden of AIV outbreaks.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述的重点是通过检查益生菌的免疫调节作用和 抗病毒药物 机制,使用益生菌减轻家禽病毒感染,特别是 禽流感 A 病毒。核心问题是益生菌是否可以作为一种有效策略,通过人畜共患 传播 来减少这些病毒对家禽健康和潜在人类健康的影响。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述使用“益生菌”、“乳杆菌”、“嗜酸菌”、“家禽”、“病毒感染”、“新城疫病毒 (NDV)”等术语和其他相关术语在 Google Scholar、Scopus 和 PubMed 上进行了文献检索。纳入标准基于与家禽益生菌干预措施的相关性、对免疫机制的关注以及对西非家禽养殖系统中常见病毒病原体的检查。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 益生菌,特别是嗜酸乳杆菌和植物乳杆菌,已显示出调节免疫参数、增强抗体反应和减少针对 禽流感 A 病毒 (AIV) 的病毒载量的潜力。这些发现表明,益生菌可能是改善家禽 AIV 免疫防御的可行策略。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该综述强调需要对益生菌针对特定 禽流感 亚型(例如 H5N1 和 H5N6)的作用进行更有针对性的研究。关于益生菌在预防人类 AIV 人畜共患 传播 方面的长期功效的证据有限,需要进一步研究来解决这些差距。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 未来的研究应优先研究益生菌对特定 禽流感 亚型的功效及其在预防人畜共患 传播 中的作用。实际应用可能包括将益生菌融入家禽养殖实践中,以增强 免疫应答 并减少 AIV 暴发 的经济和公共卫生负担。

title_zh: 益生菌作为缓解禽类病毒感染的策略:免疫调节机制与治疗潜力
source_body_en: Poultry viral infections remain a persistent challenge for the poultry industry, causing significant economic losses and posing potential threats to human health. The escalating frequency of outbreaks involving pathogens, such as infectious bronchitis virus (IBV), Newcastle disease virus (NDV) and avian influenza virus (AIV), underscores the urgent need for effective interventions. Probiotics have gained attention as a promising strategy to combat these viral infections due to their potential in enhancing immune responses and establishing a healthy gut microbiome. A literature search was carried out on Google Scholar, Scopus and PubMed using key search terms, such as 'probiotics', 'Lactobacillus', 'acidophilus', 'poultry', 'viral infections', 'Newcastle Disease Virus (NDV)' and other relevant terms. Inclusion criteria for manuscripts used were based on the relevance to probiotic-based interventions in poultry, the focus on immunological mechanisms and the examination of viral pathogens commonly found in West African poultry farming systems. This review explores the role of probiotics in mitigating the effects of NDV, AIV and IBV in poultry, focusing on their immunomodulatory effects and antiviral mechanisms. Lactobacillus acidophilus, L. plantarum have shown an interesting promise in countering NDV infections by modulating immunological parameters and enhancing antibody responses. Similarly, these probiotics have exhibited antiviral activity against AIV, promoting immune activation and reducing viral loads. plantarum have emerged as potential adjuvants for IBV vaccines, improving antibody responses and humoural immunity.
abstract_zh: 禽类病毒感染仍然是禽类养殖业中的持续挑战,导致显著的经济损失并可能对人类健康构成潜在威胁。涉及病原体的病毒感染频率不断上升,例如传染性支气管炎病毒(IBV)、新城疫病毒(NDV)和禽流感病毒(AIV),凸显了对有效干预措施的迫切需求。由于益生菌在增强免疫应答和建立健康肠道微生物群方面具有潜力,它们已成为一种有前景的策略,用于对抗这些病毒感染。通过在Google Scholar、Scopus和PubMed上使用关键搜索词,如'益生菌'、'乳酸杆菌'、'嗜酸乳杆菌'、'禽类'、'病毒感染'、'新城疫病毒(NDV)'及其他相关术语进行了文献检索。所选文献的纳入标准基于其与禽类益生菌干预措施的相关性、对免疫机制的关注以及对西非禽类养殖系统中常见病毒病原体的分析。本综述探讨了益生菌在减轻NDV、AIV和IBV对禽类影响中的作用,重点在于其免疫调节效应和抗病毒机制。嗜酸乳杆菌(Lactobacillus acidophilus)和植物乳杆菌(L. plantarum)在调节免疫参数和增强抗体反应方面显示出对抗NDV感染的有趣前景。同样,这些益生菌在对抗AIV方面也表现出抗病毒活性,促进免疫激活并降低病毒载量。植物乳杆菌在应对IBV病毒感染方面已显示出潜在的辅助作用,改善抗体反应和体液免疫。

title: Integrated HPAIV surveillance at a crane wintering site in the Izumi Plain
abstract: The Izumi Plain, Japan, is a major wintering site for endangered cranes adjacent to intensive poultry production, creating an important interface for avian influenza virus (AIV) surveillance. This Review synthesizes more than a decade of environmental and wild-bird surveillance, focusing on water collected from artificial crane roosts. Initially, virus isolation from roost water was inefficient, yielding few isolates. A modified procedure introduced in the 2018/19 season markedly improved isolation efficiency, yielding 44 low pathogenicity avian influenza viruses (LPAIVs) that season. The increased availability of infectious isolates enabled whole-genome analyses that revealed subtype diversity, reassortment, and genotype turnover, transforming roost-water surveillance from sporadic detection into a tool for characterizing AIV circulation. During the 2022/23 high pathogenicity avian influenza (HPAI) outbreak, extensive crane mortality contrasted with limited HPAIV isolation from roost water, highlighting the limitations of environmental surveillance alone. Integrating environmental, host-based, serological, and genomic data provides a more comprehensive understanding of HPAIV dynamics and strengthens surveillance at high-density wild-bird aggregation sites.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述重点关注在日本泉平原(毗邻家禽生产区)越冬的鹤中的 禽流感 A 病毒 (AIV) 及其 监测。核心问题是人工鹤栖息地的水环境 监测 如何有助于了解 AIV 循环和动态。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该评论综合了十多年的环境和野生鸟类 监测 数据,特别是从人工鹤栖息地收集的水。这些方法包括病毒分离、2018/19赛季引入的修改程序以及用于表征AIV循环的全基因组分析。

elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 在 2022/23 HPAI 暴发 期间,观察到了大量起重机 死亡率,但检测到 HPAIV 与栖息水的分离有限,突出了环境 监测 的局限性。需要集成多个数据源以更好地了解 HPAIV 动态。

title: H5N5 virus transmission is driven by repeated cross-Atlantic introductions and transmission among high latitude seabirds
abstract: In November 2025, the first global H5N5 infection was reported in a person in Washington State. Previously, these viruses had only been detected in seabirds and shorebirds near the Atlantic Ocean, suggesting potentially distinct ecology from dominant H5N1 strains. Using 354 global H5N5 genomes, we show that H5N5 viruses have been carried by high latitude seabirds and shorebirds across the Atlantic at least 9 times, with introductions more frequent in the fall and spring. We reconstruct a plausible path of cross-continental movement via Arctic or sub-Arctic regions, followed by a year of cryptic circulation prior to human spillover. These data show that H5N5 viruses have undergone far more intercontinental movements than previously recognized, and exhibit host and geographic patterns that are fundamentally distinct from dominant H5N1 lineages. The distinct host ecology, geography, and movement, paired with the capacity to infect a person, suggest that enhanced surveillance may be warranted.

title_zh: H5N5 病毒 传播 是由反复跨大西洋传入和高纬度海鸟中的 传播 驱动的
source_body_en: In November 2025, the first global H5N5 infection was reported in a person in Washington State. Previously, these viruses had only been detected in seabirds and shorebirds near the Atlantic Ocean, suggesting potentially distinct ecology from dominant H5N1 strains. Using 354 global H5N5 genomes, we show that H5N5 viruses have been carried by high latitude seabirds and shorebirds across the Atlantic at least 9 times, with introductions more frequent in the fall and spring. We reconstruct a plausible path of cross-continental movement via Arctic or sub-Arctic regions, followed by a year of cryptic circulation prior to human spillover. These data show that H5N5 viruses have undergone far more intercontinental movements than previously recognized, and exhibit host and geographic patterns that are fundamentally distinct from dominant H5N1 lineages. The distinct host ecology, geography, and movement, paired with the capacity to infect a person, suggest that enhanced surveillance may be warranted.

title: Silent travelers: the potential of migratory birds and their ticks to introduce emerging viruses into Switzerland
abstract: Abstract Switzerland hosts over 400 bird species, many of which are migratory. Through diverse movement patterns, ranging from short distances to almost global migrations, these birds can introduce zoonotic viruses, such as West Nile virus (WNV) or avian influenza virus (AIV), as well as unknown and potentially emerging viruses. Furthermore, they facilitate the global dispersal of infected ectoparasites, particularly ticks, risking the introduction of novel tick-borne diseases. To assess this risk, we sampled 42 bird species (39 migratory, 3 resident) over seven months in 2023 at the Bolle di Magadino nature reserve and the Piano di Magadino area in the canton Ticino (Switzerland). This region, because of its transitional climate, serves as an important resting and breeding ground for migratory birds. In total, 496 oropharyngeal-cloacal swabs, 164 sera, and 22 associated ticks were collected. While RT-qPCR of the swabs detected no active WNV or AIV infections, ELISA testing identified Orthoflavivirus antibodies in 15 of 164 sera, indicating prior exposure. Metagenomic next-generation sequencing revealed a viral landscape spanning 33 families (29 of which were identified in birds). Within this virome, DNA viruses, predominantly Circoviridae, Genomoviridae, and Parvoviridae , dominated in abundance but exhibited low diversity. In contrast, the highly diverse RNA virome primarily reflected the birds’ dietary habits and the local habitat at the nature reserve. Notably, we report the first detection of Bole tick virus 4 (BoTV4) in Switzerland, identified in several ticks ( Rhipicephalus turanicus ) associated with long-distance migrants. This member of the newly established Pestiviridae family is already established in parts of Asia, Africa, and Europe. This study provides the first active surveillance of the wild bird virome in Switzerland. Our findings establish a framework for the early detection of emerging viruses and underscore the role of migratory birds as dispersal vectors for ticks and novel tick-borne viruses.

title_zh: 沉默的旅行者:候鸟及其蜱虫将新出现的病毒引入瑞士的潜力
source_body_en: Abstract Switzerland hosts over 400 bird species, many of which are migratory. Through diverse movement patterns, ranging from short distances to almost global migrations, these birds can introduce zoonotic viruses, such as West Nile virus (WNV) or avian influenza virus (AIV), as well as unknown and potentially emerging viruses. Furthermore, they facilitate the global dispersal of infected ectoparasites, particularly ticks, risking the introduction of novel tick-borne diseases. To assess this risk, we sampled 42 bird species (39 migratory, 3 resident) over seven months in 2023 at the Bolle di Magadino nature reserve and the Piano di Magadino area in the canton Ticino (Switzerland). This region, because of its transitional climate, serves as an important resting and breeding ground for migratory birds. In total, 496 oropharyngeal-cloacal swabs, 164 sera, and 22 associated ticks were collected. While RT-qPCR of the swabs detected no active WNV or AIV infections, ELISA testing identified Orthoflavivirus antibodies in 15 of 164 sera, indicating prior exposure. Metagenomic next-generation sequencing revealed a viral landscape spanning 33 families (29 of which were identified in birds). Within this virome, DNA viruses, predominantly Circoviridae, Genomoviridae, and Parvoviridae , dominated in abundance but exhibited low diversity. In contrast, the highly diverse RNA virome primarily reflected the birds’ dietary habits and the local habitat at the nature reserve. Notably, we report the first detection of Bole tick virus 4 (BoTV4) in Switzerland, identified in several ticks ( Rhipicephalus turanicus ) associated with long-distance migrants. This member of the newly established Pestiviridae family is already established in parts of Asia, Africa, and Europe. This study provides the first active surveillance of the wild bird virome in Switzerland. Our findings establish a framework for the early detection of emerging viruses and underscore the role of migratory birds as dispersal vectors for ticks and novel tick-borne viruses.
abstract_zh: 摘要 瑞士 宿主 有 400 多种鸟类,其中许多是候鸟。通过不同的运动模式,从短距离到几乎全球性的迁徙,这些鸟类可以引入人畜共患病毒,例如西尼罗河病毒(WNV)或禽流感病毒(AIV),以及未知和潜在新出现的病毒。此外,它们还促进了受感染的体外寄生虫(尤其是蜱虫)在全球的传播,从而带来了引入新型蜱传疾病的风险。为了评估这种风险,我们在 2023 年的七个月内对提契诺州(瑞士)的 Bolle di Magadino 自然保护区和 Piano di Magadino 地区的 42 种鸟类(39 种候鸟,3 种留鸟)进行了采样。该地区气候过渡,是候鸟的重要休息和繁殖地。总共收集了 496 份口咽泄殖腔拭子、164 份血清和 22 只相关蜱。虽然拭子的 RT-qPCR 没有检测到活跃的 WNV 或 AIV 感染,但 ELISA 测试在 164 份血清中的 15 份中发现了正黄病毒抗体,表明之前曾接触过。宏基因组下一代测序揭示了跨越 33 个科的病毒景观(其中 29 个科是在鸟类中发现的)。在该病毒组中,DNA病毒(主要是圆环病毒科、基因病毒科和细小病毒科)在丰度上占主导地位,但表现出较低的多样性。相比之下,高度多样化的RNA病毒组主要反映了鸟类的饮食习惯和自然保护区的当地栖息地。值得注意的是,我们报告在瑞士首次检测到伯乐蜱病毒 4 (BoTV4),该病毒在与长途迁徙有关的几种蜱 (Rhipicephalus turanicus) 中被发现。这种新建立的瘟病毒科成员已经在亚洲、非洲和欧洲的部分地区定居。这项研究提供了瑞士第一个活跃的 野生鸟类 病毒组 监测。我们的研究结果为早期检测新出现的病毒建立了一个框架,并强调了候鸟作为蜱虫和新型蜱传病毒传播 媒介 的作用。

title: Bovine-Associated Viruses at the Human–Animal Interface: Zoonotic Risks, Spillover Dynamics, and One Health Implications
abstract: Cattle serve as critical ecological reservoirs and amplifying hosts for numerous zoonotic viruses, thereby playing a central role in their maintenance, evolution, and interspecies transmission. Here, we briefly evaluate six viral pathogens of significant public health relevance linked to cattle, namely cowpox virus, bovine coronavirus, influenza A virus (H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b), bovine rotavirus, bovine leukemia virus, and SARS-CoV-2. This review focuses on advances in viral characterization, host tropism, and the mechanisms that may facilitate spillover through routes such as direct contact, environmental exposure, and foodborne transmission. It further highlights the bidirectional nature of pathogen exchange at the human-animal interface, where cattle may act as a source of viral variants with potential public health implications, though the risk varies considerably among the viruses discussed. Moreover, we discuss the imperative for integrated surveillance and One Health interventions to mitigate these transmission risks, highlighting cattle as valuable sentinel species within global health security frameworks.

This review focuses on advances in viral characterization, host tropism, and the mechanisms that may facilitate spillover through routes such as direct contact, environmental exposure, and foodborne transmission. It further highlights the bidirectional nature of pathogen exchange at the human-animal interface, where cattle may act as a source of viral variants with potential public health implications, though the risk varies considerably among the viruses discussed. Moreover, we discuss the imperative for integrated surveillance and One Health interventions to mitigate these transmission risks, highlighting cattle as valuable sentinel species within global health security frameworks.
title_original: Bovine-Associated Viruses at the Human–Animal Interface: Zoonotic Risks, Spillover Dynamics, and One Health Implications

analysis.scope_and_question: Avian influenza A viruses, avian-origin zoonotic infections, and qualified avian subtypes are the focus of this review. The central question is to explore the zoonotic risks, spillover dynamics, and One Health implications of these viruses at the human–animal interface.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review evaluates six viral pathogens of significant public health relevance linked to cattle, including avian influenza A virus (H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b). The evidence is derived from the abstract, which outlines the review's focus on viral characterization, host tropism, and spillover mechanisms. The review does not explicitly report on meta-analysis or consensus processes.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review highlights that avian influenza A viruses, particularly H5N1, are critical in maintaining and evolving zoonotic viruses. It emphasizes the role of cattle as ecological reservoirs and amplifying hosts for these viruses, contributing to their interspecies transmission. The review also underscores the importance of understanding the bidirectional nature of pathogen exchange at the human–animal interface.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes that the risk of avian influenza A viruses spilling over into humans varies considerably among the viruses discussed. There is a lack of detailed information on the specific mechanisms of spillover and the extent of transmission through different routes such as direct contact, environmental exposure, and foodborne transmission.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review calls for integrated surveillance and One Health interventions to mitigate the transmission risks of avian influenza A viruses. It emphasizes the need for further research on the mechanisms of spillover and the development of targeted strategies to monitor and control these viruses in both animal and human populations.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the zoonotic risks, spillover dynamics, and One Health implications of avian influenza A viruses at the human–animal interface. It highlights the role of cattle as ecological reservoirs and amplifying hosts for these viruses, contributing to their maintenance, evolution, and interspecies transmission. The review evaluates six viral pathogens, including H5N1, and discusses the bidirectional nature of pathogen exchange. It identifies evidence gaps in understanding specific spillover mechanisms and emphasizes the need for integrated surveillance and interventions to mitigate transmission risks. The review underscores the importance of studying avian influenza A viruses to enhance global health security.

abstract_zh: 牛是许多人畜共患病毒的重要生态储存宿主和放大宿主,从而在其维持、进化和种间传播中发挥核心作用。在这里,我们简要评估了与牛相关的六种具有重要公共卫生相关性的病毒病原体,即牛痘病毒、牛冠状病毒、甲型流感病毒(H5N1 进化枝 2.3.4.4b)、牛轮状病毒、牛白血病病毒和 SARS-CoV-2。本综述重点关注病毒特征、宿主 向性以及可能通过直接接触、环境暴露和食源性 传播 等途径促进 跨物种溢出 的机制。它进一步强调了人与动物界面上病原体交换的双向性质,其中牛可能充当具有潜在公共卫生影响的病毒变异体的来源,尽管所讨论的病毒之间的风险差异很大。此外,我们讨论了综合 监测 和 One Health 干预措施以减轻这些 传播 风险的必要性,强调牛是全球健康安全框架内有价值的哨兵物种。

title: Defective Viral Genomes Reveal History-dependent Self-regulation of Type I Interferon Dynamics
abstract: Abstract Type I interferons (IFN) help clear a viral infection, but IFN levels can then decline to reset the antiviral state and avoid innate immune dysregulation. Such dysregulation can occur following infection with highly pathogenic and pandemic RNA viruses, such as H5N1 influenza A viruses or SARS-CoV-2. In spite of the strong innate immune response that these viruses induce, pandemic viruses replicate and spread successfully, suggesting that they can circumvent the effects of IFN. Innate immune activation is triggered when host cells detect viral RNA, especially defective viral genomes (DVGs). A strong IFN response (e.g. to DVGs or a highly immunogenic wild-type infection) must then decline through negative feedback involving the IFN receptor. How DVGs modulate this feedback remains poorly understood. To quantify positive and negative IFN regulation, we first performed in vitro experiments combining different doses of viral RNA and exogenous IFN, and measured subsequent IFN expression. We next developed an in vivo Bayesian computational model that captures the impact of influenza virus DVGs on both positive and negative IFN feedback. Competition between DVGs and virus is also considered. Finally, we calibrated this model on published in vitro and in vivo influenza virus infection data. Our model suggests that the cumulative IFN exposure of a host cell, rather than the instantaneous IFN level, shapes further IFN induction; this gives DVGs a dual role: beyond triggering IFN induction, they can also lower it through negative feedback. Our model further predicts that these effects are important locally, shaping the spatial dynamics of the response, allowing suppression of innate immune responses in neighbouring, uninfected cells. Through this model, we can explain two important biological observations: i) IFN levels can decline while virus and DVG levels continue to rise in tissue culture and mouse infections; and ii) pandemic viruses that produce high levels of immunogenic RNA molecules can successfully replicate through local innate immune suppression. Overall, we propose that heterogeneity within viral populations (including DVGs and other noncanonical viral RNAs) can modulate positive and negative feedback loops and shape infection outcomes. More broadly, our work may support studies into the therapeutic use of these viral RNA populations. Author summary Humans and animals have to fight influenza virus and other infections without inducing immunopathology. After detection of an infection, the innate immune system produces type I interferon (IFN), a signal that starts a protective response. However, high levels of IFN and prolonged IFN expression can cause damage to tissues and worsen disease. Negative feedback is one route by which IFN production can stop, but its activation during viral infection remains poorly understood. A central question is why viruses can continue to replicate and spread despite a strong IFN response. We here investigated why IFN levels can begin to decline while virus levels continue to rise during influenza virus infection. This decline is most pronounced when the virus produces large amounts of defective viral genomes (DVGs). These defective genomes arise naturally during viral replication and are produced by many RNA viruses, including SARS-CoV-2, Ebola virus, and measles virus. Using cell-culture experiments, computational modelling, and fitting of our model to cell-culture and mouse data, we find that defective genomes contribute to both IFN activation and its negative feedback. Both the experiments and model support a mechanism in which IFN accumulation during infection suppresses its own production, and that this suppression can start earlier under strong DVG stimulation. At the local level, this can allow viral spread to continue even while overall IFN levels remain high. Overall, our findings reveal an additional level of interplay between defective viral genomes and the host innate immune system. They also suggest that the potential therapeutic use of defective genomes must be carefully calibrated to achieve an optimal antiviral response.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to understand how type I interferon (IFN) dynamics are regulated during viral infections, particularly focusing on the role of defective viral genomes (DVGs) in modulating IFN responses. The background highlights that IFN levels can decline despite strong innate immune responses, which is critical for avoiding immunopathology.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study combined in vitro experiments with an in vivo Bayesian computational model to investigate the impact of influenza virus DVGs on IFN feedback. It used published in vitro and in vivo influenza virus infection data for calibration.
analysis.methods: The researchers conducted in vitro experiments with varying doses of viral RNA and exogenous IFN to measure IFN expression. They also developed a computational model to simulate the effects of DVGs on IFN feedback and calibrated it using existing infection data.
analysis.main_results: The model suggests that cumulative IFN exposure, rather than instantaneous levels, shapes further IFN induction. DVGs are shown to trigger IFN activation while also contributing to negative feedback, which can suppress innate immune responses in neighboring cells.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings reveal a dual role of DVGs in both activating and suppressing IFN responses, offering a novel mechanism for how viruses can evade immune responses. This explains two key observations: IFN levels can decline while virus levels rise, and pandemic viruses can replicate through local immune suppression.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results provide insights into the complex interplay between DVGs and the host immune system, which could inform strategies for therapeutic interventions targeting viral RNA populations to optimize antiviral responses.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study relies on in vitro and in vivo data, which may limit generalizability. However, the model is calibrated on published data, and the evidence is supported by both experimental and computational approaches, giving it a moderate confidence level.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates how defective viral genomes (DVGs) influence type I interferon (IFN) dynamics during influenza virus infection. The research highlights that DVGs can both trigger IFN induction and contribute to negative feedback, allowing viruses to evade immune responses. By combining in vitro experiments with a Bayesian computational model, the authors demonstrate that cumulative IFN exposure, rather than instantaneous levels, determines further IFN production. Their findings explain why IFN levels can decline while virus levels rise and suggest that DVGs may play a role in local immune suppression, which could have implications for antiviral therapies. The study's reliance on existing data limits its generalizability, but the integration of experimental and computational methods provides a moderate level of confidence in its conclusions.

elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果提供了对 DVG 和 宿主 免疫系统之间复杂相互作用的见解,这可以为针对病毒 RNA 群体的治疗干预策略提供信息,以优化 抗病毒药物 反应。

abstract_zh: 摘要 I 型干扰素 (IFN) 有助于清除病毒感染,但 IFN 水平可能会下降,从而重置 抗病毒药物 状态并避免先天免疫失调。这种失调可能发生在感染高致病性和大流行性 RNA 病毒(例如 H5N1 甲型流感病毒或 SARS-CoV-2)后。尽管这些病毒诱导出强大的先天 免疫应答,但大流行病毒仍能成功复制和传播,这表明它们可以规避 IFN 的影响。当 宿主 细胞检测到病毒 RNA,尤其是有缺陷的病毒 基因组 (DVG) 时,会触发先天免疫激活。然后,强烈的 IFN 反应(例如对 DVG 或高免疫原性野生型感染)必须通过涉及 IFN 受体的负反馈而减弱。DVG 如何调节这种反馈仍然知之甚少。为了量化IFN的正向和负向调节,我们首先结合不同剂量的病毒RNA和外源IFN进行体外实验,并测量随后的IFN表达。接下来,我们开发了一种体内贝叶斯计算模型,该模型可以捕获流感病毒 DVG 对 IFN 正反馈和负反馈的影响。还考虑了 DVG 和病毒之间的竞争。最后,我们根据已发表的体外和体内流感病毒感染数据校准了该模型。我们的模型表明,宿主 细胞的累积 IFN 暴露,而不是瞬时 IFN 水平,决定了进一步的 IFN 诱导;这赋予 DVG 双重作用:除了触发 IFN 诱导之外,它们还可以通过负反馈降低 IFN 诱导。我们的模型进一步预测这些效应在局部很重要,塑造了反应的空间动态,从而抑制邻近未感染细胞中的先天 免疫应答。通过这个模型,我们可以解释两个重要的生物学观察结果:i)在组织培养和小鼠感染中,IFN 水平可能下降,而病毒和 DVG 水平继续上升;ii) 产生高水平免疫原性 RNA 分子的大流行病毒可以通过局部先天免疫抑制成功复制。总体而言,我们认为病毒群体内的异质性(包括 DVG 和其他非典型病毒 RNA)可以调节正反馈环和负反馈环并塑造感染结果。更广泛地说,我们的工作可能支持这些病毒 RNA 群体的治疗用途的研究。作者摘要 人类和动物必须在不引发免疫病理学的情况下对抗流感病毒和其他感染。检测到感染后,先天免疫系统会产生 I 型干扰素 (IFN),这是一种启动保护性反应的信号。然而,高水平的干扰素和延长的干扰素表达会导致组织损伤并使疾病恶化。负反馈是干扰素产生停止的一种途径,但其在病毒感染期间的激活仍知之甚少。一个核心问题是,为什么尽管有强烈的干扰素反应,病毒仍能继续复制和传播。我们在这里研究了为什么在流感病毒感染期间,干扰素水平会开始下降,而病毒水平继续上升。当病毒产生大量有缺陷的病毒 基因组 (DVG) 时,这种下降最为明显。这些有缺陷的 基因组 在病毒复制过程中自然出现,由许多 RNA 病毒产生,包括 SARS-CoV-2、埃博拉病毒和麻疹病毒。通过细胞培养实验、计算建模以及将我们的模型与细胞培养和小鼠数据进行拟合,我们发现有缺陷的 基因组 会导致 IFN 激活及其负反馈。实验和模型都支持感染过程中 IFN 积累抑制其自身产生的机制,并且这种抑制可以在强 DVG 刺激下更早开始。在地方层面,即使总体干扰素水平仍然很高,这也可能导致病毒继续传播。总体而言,我们的研究结果揭示了有缺陷的病毒 基因组 和 宿主 先天免疫系统之间的额外相互作用。他们还建议,必须仔细校准有缺陷的 基因组 的潜在治疗用途,以实现最佳的 抗病毒药物 反应。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在了解病毒感染期间 I 型干扰素 (IFN) 动态如何受到调节,特别关注有缺陷的病毒 基因组 (DVG) 在调节 IFN 反应中的作用。背景强调,尽管先天 免疫应答 很强,但 IFN 水平仍可能下降,这对于避免免疫病理学至关重要。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究将体外实验与体内贝叶斯计算模型相结合,研究流感病毒 DVG 对 IFN 反馈的影响。它使用已发表的体外和体内流感病毒感染数据进行校准。
analysis_zh.methods: 研究人员用不同剂量的病毒RNA和外源干扰素进行了体外实验,以测量干扰素的表达。他们还开发了一个计算模型来模拟 DVG 对 IFN 反馈的影响,并使用现有的感染数据对其进行校准。
analysis_zh.main_results: 该模型表明,累积的干扰素暴露,而不是瞬时水平,决定了进一步的干扰素诱导。DVG 被证明可以触发 IFN 激活,同时也有助于负反馈,从而抑制邻近细胞中先天的 免疫应答。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果揭示了 DVG 在激活和抑制 IFN 反应中的双重作用,为病毒如何逃避 免疫应答 提供了一种新机制。这解释了两个关键的观察结果:当病毒水平上升时,干扰素水平可能下降,大流行病毒可以通过局部免疫抑制进行复制。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果提供了对 DVG 和 宿主 免疫系统之间复杂相互作用的见解,这可以为针对病毒 RNA 群体的治疗干预策略提供信息,以优化 抗病毒药物 反应。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究依赖于体外和体内数据,这可能会限制普遍性。然而,该模型是根据已发布的数据进行校准的,并且证据得到实验和计算方法的支持,使其具有中等的置信度。

title: Epitope-guided optimization improves the protective efficacy of NA-based mRNA vaccines against seasonal influenza A(H3N2) virus.
abstract: Neuraminidase (NA) is increasingly recognized as a promising target antigen for improving the breadth and durability of influenza vaccines, yet NA-based mRNA vaccines remain comparatively unexplored relative to hemagglutinin-based approaches. Here, we applied a computationally guided NA antigen-design strategy to seasonal H3N2 influenza viruses and investigated whether epitope-guided optimization could improve the immunogenicity and protective efficacy of NA-based mRNA vaccines. NA-D3, an NA antigen designed based on the evolutionary characteristics of circulating H3N2 viruses, was first evaluated in an mRNA vaccine. This vaccine provided partial protection against H3N2 challenge and reduced viral replication in the lungs, although detectable neuraminidase inhibition (NAI) activity was not observed. To further improve NA antigen immunogenicity, predicted B- and T-cell epitopes were incorporated into the antigen design process, resulting in three sequentially optimized NA candidates, F0, F1, and F2. In a subsequent challenge experiment, F1 and F2 conferred complete protection, achieving 100% survival and significantly lower viral RNA levels and infectious viral titers in the lungs compared to controls. The optimized NA mRNA vaccines also induced detectable NAI activity against heterologous H3N2 viruses, albeit at relatively modest levels. Collectively, these findings demonstrate the protective potential of NA-based mRNA vaccination against H3N2 influenza viruses and establish iterative, epitope-guided strategy in NA antigen optimization - integrating computational prediction with experimental validation - as an effective approach for developing broadly protective NA-based mRNA vaccines.

title: Pathogenicity and zoonotic potential of a novel pdm09-lineage H1N2 swine influenza A virus spatiotemporally linked to transboundary pig trade
abstract: International swine trade can disseminate influenza A viruses across borders, creating opportunities for reassortment with endemic swine viruses and the emergence of novel strains with zoonotic potential. Here, we characterize a novel H1N2 reassortant, A/swine/Korea/1030-3/2023 (1030-3), detected in South Korea and spatiotemporally associated with European swine lineages and international pig movement. 1030-3 harbors seven gene segments (PB2, PB1, PA, HA, NP, M and NS) closely related to a recent Danish zoonotic H1N1 virus of the 2009 pandemic (pdm09) lineage, and an N2 segment derived from an endemic Korean HxN2. In vitro assays demonstrated that 1030-3 preferentially bound human-type α2,6-linked sialic acid receptors and replicated efficiently in polarized human airway epithelial cells, although these properties were also observed in the endemic Korean H1N2 comparator 1027-1. In mice, 1030-3 caused moderate clinical signs and respiratory replication comparable to an early pdm09 reference strain NL09. In guinea pigs, 1030-3 transmitted to a subset of direct-contact animals but showed no detectable aerosol transmission under the conditions tested. In pigs, the natural host, 1030-3 replicated efficiently and transmitted to all direct-contact animals, with high respiratory shedding and a greater cumulative shedding burden in contact pigs than NL09. Contemporary human sera showed reduced neutralizing activity against 1030-3 relative to both human seasonal H1N1 and 1027-1, while antiserum against a recent H1N1 vaccine antigen also neutralized 1030-3 less efficiently. These findings identify a European-associated H1N2 swine influenza reassortant detected in South Korea that combines a distinct pdm09-derived genomic and antigenic background with efficient replication and transmission in pigs, α2,6-linked receptor preference, and reduced neutralization by human sera, underscoring the need for trade-aware surveillance of swIAVs and continued monitoring at the swine-human interface.

source_records.abstract: International swine trade can disseminate influenza A viruses across borders, creating opportunities for reassortment with endemic swine viruses and the emergence of novel strains with zoonotic potential. Here, we characterize a novel H1N2 reassortant, A/swine/Korea/1030-3/2023 (1030-3), detected in South Korea and spatiotemporally associated with European swine lineages and international pig movement. 1030-3 harbors seven gene segments (PB2, PB1, PA, HA, NP, M and NS) closely related to a recent Danish zoonotic H1N1 virus of the 2009 pandemic (pdm09) lineage, and an N2 segment derived from an endemic Korean HxN2. In vitro assays demonstrated that 1030-3 preferentially bound human-type α2,6-linked sialic acid receptors and replicated efficiently in polarized human airway epithelial cells, although these properties were also observed in the endemic Korean H1N2 comparator 1027-1. In mice, 1030-3 caused moderate clinical signs and respiratory replication comparable to an early pdm09 reference strain NL09. In guinea pigs, 1030-3 transmitted to a subset of direct-contact animals but showed no detectable aerosol transmission under the conditions tested. In pigs, the natural host, 1030-3 replicated efficiently and transmitted to all direct-contact animals, with high respiratory shedding and a greater cumulative shedding burden in contact pigs than NL09. Contemporary human sera showed reduced neutralizing activity against 1030-3 relative to both human seasonal H1N1 and 1027-1, while antiserum against a recent H1N1 vaccine antigen also neutralized 1030-3 less efficiently. These findings identify a European-associated H1N2 swine influenza reassortant detected in South Korea that combines a distinct pdm09-derived genomic and antigenic background with efficient replication and transmission in pigs, α2,6-linked receptor preference, and reduced neutralization by human sera, underscoring the need for trade-aware surveillance of swIAVs and continued monitoring at the swine-human interface.

title: Influenza thermostability
abstract: Even prior to the advent of germ theory in the 19th century, disease inflicted by viruses and the scale at which this could occur was recognised and feared, if not understood. Some viruses, such as influenza A virus (IAV), have been the cause of great morbidity and mortality throughout history. Their ability to transmit between hosts is key to their pandemic potential. This is not trivial, requiring the virus to surmount a veritable obstacle course of environmental insults before reaching safe harbour; a compatible host organism. Surprisingly, this area is relatively unstudied, with a dearth of clarity on how this occurs, and perhaps most importantly, the bounds of virus viability. Temperature is one of the key environmental factors of viral stability. Exploited as a means of pathogen eradication throughout history, likely predating any concept of micro-organisms, it remains in use today, particularly in the food and healthcare industry, e.g pasteurisation. Fortunately this process remains effective against IAV, reassuring when avian influenza spread to dairy cattle. Understanding the mechanism of viral inactivation due to heat would allow us to improve the efficacy of disinfection via this method and likely have other applications, for example in vaccine stability. This study is an effort to disentangle the complex environmental factors by focusing on thermostability in bulk solution. It found that IAV infectivity demonstrated first-order exponential decay below 50 °C, indicating a non-cooperative inactivation mechanism. Arrhenius behaviour between two linear regimes (above and below 40 °C) suggest there are different dominant inactivation pathways separated by temperature. The 40-50 °C regime was further elucidated in view of its implications on disinfection. Thermodynamic analysis suggests a process consistent with protein unfolding, particularly implicating the viral haemagglutinin (HA). Alternative inactivation mechanisms such as virion rupture, aggregation or failure of receptor binding were excluded. Modifications to HA, such as amino-acid substitution or prevention of cleavage, resulted in an increased inactivation rate, and alterations to thermodynamic parameters. Lowering the pH had a similar effect on rate, but also lowered the energy barrier for viral inactivation, hinting at a catalytic process. A 3-state mathematical model of HA conformational change was able to recapitulate experimental findings at both low and neutral pH, suggesting the transitions are key to the underlying mechanism. Although the precise point of failure remains unclear, potential causes include insertion of the HA fusion peptide into an inappropriate target membrane. This work presents areas for further investigation and a way to translate these methods and approach to identify inactivation mechanisms in other pathogens.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to understand the mechanism of viral inactivation due to heat, particularly in the context of influenza A virus (IAV), which has historically caused significant morbidity and mortality. The background highlights the importance of understanding how viruses maintain viability in the face of environmental challenges.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study focused on thermostability in bulk solution, examining the inactivation of IAV under varying temperature conditions. It was conducted as part of a dissertation at the University of Edinburgh, published on 2026-11-04.
analysis.methods: The study employed thermodynamic analysis and a 3-state mathematical model of HA conformational change to investigate the inactivation mechanisms of IAV. It also examined modifications to HA, such as amino-acid substitution or prevention of cleavage, to assess their impact on inactivation rates.
analysis.main_results: The study found that IAV infectivity demonstrated first-order exponential decay below 50 °C, indicating a non-cooperative inactivation mechanism. Arrhenius behaviour between two linear regimes (above and below 40 °C) suggests different dominant inactivation pathways separated by temperature.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that the inactivation of IAV at 40-50 °C is consistent with protein unfolding, particularly implicating the viral haemagglutinin (HA). This provides novel insights into the temperature-dependent stability of IAV and its implications for disinfection methods.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Understanding the mechanism of viral inactivation due to heat can improve the efficacy of disinfection protocols and have broader applications, such as enhancing vaccine stability.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on abstract-only evidence, which may limit the depth of analysis. However, the findings are supported by thermodynamic analysis and mathematical modeling, providing a moderate level of confidence in the conclusions.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the thermostability of influenza A virus (IAV) in bulk solution, focusing on the mechanisms of heat-induced inactivation. The research highlights the importance of understanding how IAV maintains viability under environmental stress, particularly in the context of its pandemic potential. The study found that IAV infectivity decreases exponentially below 50 °C, suggesting a non-cooperative inactivation mechanism. Thermodynamic analysis and a 3-state mathematical model of HA conformational change were used to elucidate these findings, indicating that protein unfolding, especially of HA, plays a key role. The results have implications for improving disinfection methods and vaccine stability. While the study is based on abstract-only evidence, the findings are supported by modeling and analysis, offering a moderate level of confidence. The research contributes to the understanding of IAV's environmental resilience and provides a framework for further investigations into other pathogens.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在了解热导致病毒失活的机制,特别是在甲型流感病毒 (IAV) 的背景下,该病毒历来导致显着的发病率和 死亡率。这一背景凸显了了解病毒在面对环境挑战时如何保持活力的重要性。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究重点考察了 bulk 溶液中的热稳定性,分析了在不同温度条件下 IAV 的失活情况。该研究是爱丁堡大学博士论文的一部分,发表于 2026-11-04。
elements_zh.methods: 本研究采用热力学分析和HA构象变化的3态数学模型来探讨IAV失活机制。同时,还考察了HA的修饰,如氨基酸替换或切割位点的阻断,以评估它们对失活速率的影响。
elements_zh.main_results: 研究发现,IAV 感染力在 50°C 以下表现出一级指数衰减,表明存在非合作灭活机制。两个线性状态(高于和低于 40 °C)之间的阿伦尼乌斯行为表明,不同的主要失活途径因温度而分开。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,IAV 在 40-50 °C 时失活与蛋白质解折叠一致,特别是与病毒血凝素 (HA) 相关。这为 IAV 的温度依赖性稳定性及其对消毒方法的影响提供了新的见解。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 了解热导致病毒灭活的机制可以提高消毒方案的功效并具有更广泛的应用,例如增强 疫苗 的稳定性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅基于抽象证据,这可能会限制分析的深度。然而,这些发现得到了热力学分析和数学模型的支持,为结论提供了中等程度的可信度。

title: Diagnóstico de hemoparásitos, enteroparásitos y virus de importancia zoonótica en poblaciones urbanas de Columba livia en Colombia
abstract: Domestic pigeons (Columba livia) are reservoirs of several infectious agents and represent a risk to public health. In Colombia, this introduced species is common in urban areas, where several microbiological studies have been conducted. However, its role in circulating West Nile virus (WNV) and avian influenza (AI) remains unknown. This study aimed to evaluate the presence of enteroparasites, haemoparasites, and the detection of WNV and AI in feral pigeons captured in Bogotá, Arauca and Aguazul. Faecal samples, blood samples, oral and cloacal swabs were collected from 48 individuals. Parasitological analyses included fresh examination for gastrointestinal parasites and Giemsa staining for haemoparasites. RT-qPCR was used to detect the virus using TaqMan and SYBR-Green. The results indicate the presence of Haemoproteus columbae, together with the presence of several endoparasites, including Eimeria and Blastocystis, among others, in Arauca and Bogota. We discuss the results of molecular testing for potentially zoonotic viruses. Continued active surveillance in synanthropic species such as this one is essential to establish prevention and control strategies in urban contexts, where frequent contact between humans and pigeons may facilitate the transmission of microorganisms.

title: ADAR-mediated RNA editing of Influenza A virus genomes may be age-dependent and inversely correlates with viral load
abstract: Background Seasonal influenza epidemics cause significant mortality, especially among the elderly. Influenza A virus triggers the host innate immune system through various mechanisms. Human enzymes belonging to the group of RNA-acting adenosine deaminases (ADARs) play a role in the innate antiviral immune response, partly by inducing mutations in viral RNA. The effect of this mechanismin influenza A virus infection remains unexplained in humans.Objective The aim of this study was to assess the clinical impact of ADAR-induced mutations on influenza A virus in hospitalised patients.Methods Full-genome deep sequencing of Influenza A virus was performed on respiratory samples from 75 hospitalised, Influenza A(H3N2) virus infected patients, aged 41 to 95 years. ADAR-associated mutations in minor viral subpopulations were analysed in relation to demographic and clinical factors.Results ADAR-associated mutations showed a significant inverse correlation with viral load (p < 0.0001) and age (p = 0.0051), especially in patients older than 75 years. The association between ADAR-associated mutations and viral load was independent of age, inflammation, and disease severity (p < 0.001).Conclusions We found an association between ADAR-induced mutations and viral load, which may indicate an antiviral function of ADAR on influenza A virus. The lower mutation rate and associated higher viral load in the elderly suggest an age-dependent reduced ADAR activity, which may contribute to increased disease severity.

title: Cross-reactivity against drifted influenza A (H3N2) subclade K is predicted by pre-existing antibody signatures from recent vaccine targets
abstract: Abstract Seasonal influenza vaccine strains are selected months before the flu season begins, risking a vaccine mismatch. To that end, quickly predicting protection against newly emerged influenza strains is a public health preparedness need. Further, understanding immunological correlates of protection against mismatched targets is necessary for improving annual influenza vaccination compositions and/or platforms. Using a modified systems-predicted neutralizing antibody (SNAb) approach, we quantified predicted influenza virus neutralization responses in a human cohort pre- and post-vaccination during the 2025/2026 influenza season, during which the vaccine-mismatched H3N2 subclade K accounted for most influenza virus infections. This was done using the previous 10 years of vaccine targets, including the components of the 2025/2026 vaccination, as well as the 2026/2027 vaccine targets. We identified that H3N2 subclade K responders were predicted by baseline SNAb profiles, particularly to the H3N2 components of the 2024/2025 and 2025/2026 influenza vaccine. Systems serological analysis supported this at the multivariate level, with even greater accuracy in predicting mismatched responses from pre-vaccination humoral signatures. Lastly, we employed this approach to predict who would likely be high responders to the 2026/2027 influenza vaccine H1 component, and found that antibody features selected as predicting a strong neutralization response were disproportionately enriched for the H1 component of the 2025/2026 influenza vaccination. Our results support a model in which systems-based approaches can identify signatures predicting strong influenza vaccination responses before the influenza season begins.

title: Breaking the channel barrier: same-fluorescence, different-Tm probe strategy enables seven-target respiratory virus detection on a six-channel PCR platform within 20 minutes.
abstract: BACKGROUND Respiratory pathogens with overlapping symptoms-including SARS-CoV-2, influenza A/B, H5/H7/H10 avian influenza, and RSV-co-circulate and co-infect, demanding rapid multiplex screening at points of care. Conventional multiplex real-time PCR is constrained by hardware channel capacity (≤6), making it difficult to detect seven targets while distinguishing influenza A and B in a single tube. This work addresses the contradiction between high-order multiplexing and limited fluorescence channels without sacrificing speed or sensitivity. RESULTS We developed a six-channel ultra-fast PCR platform detecting seven respiratory viruses in a single tube within 20 min, using a same-fluorescence, different-Tm probe strategy. Influenza A and B share the FAM channel yet generate distinct melting peaks (∼12 °C difference, 84.8 °C vs. 72.3 °C), enabling accurate typing via melting curve analysis. Primers, probes, and enzymes are pre-embedded as lyophilized beads in sealed cartridges for fully automated sample-to-result operation. The assay achieved 100% detection at 5 copies/test for all targets, linearity (R2 > 0.95) across 5-105 copies/test, 90-110% efficiencies, and no cross-reactivity against 39 non-target pathogens. Cartridges remained stable for 12 months at 25 °C. Validation on 271 clinical specimens showed 100% agreement with sequencing-verified single-plex qPCR. SIGNIFICANCE AND NOVELTY This work provides the first integration of melting-curve-based same-channel multiplexing with lyophilized cartridge technology on an ultra-fast PCR platform. By overcoming channel limitations while maintaining speed and sensitivity, the system offers a practical, field-deployable screening tool for decentralized respiratory pathogen detection in resource-limited settings.

title: Rapid UAV-based detection of crane (Grus grus) mortality hotspots during an H5N1 avian influenza outbreak using deep learning
abstract: Rapid detection of wildlife mortality during infectious disease outbreaks is essential for ecological risk mitigation, zoonotic-risk management, and timely intervention, yet field surveys are often slow, labor-intensive, and spatially limited. This study evaluates unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery combined with deep learning as an operational surveillance tool for mapping live and deceased Common Cranes ( Grus grus ) during a highly pathogenic avian influenza (H5N1) outbreak in the Hula Valley, Israel. High-resolution RGB imagery was collected over aquatic roosting and terrestrial feeding habitats and annotated to distinguish living and dead individuals. A YOLOv8-based detection framework was tested using habitat-specific training, combined multi-habitat training, and transfer learning from a large avian dataset, together with selective data augmentation, sliding-window inference, and Weighted Boxes Fusion. Living cranes were detected reliably across habitats, with AP@50 reaching 0.89 in mosaicked feeding-area imagery and 0.98 in raw feeding-area imagery. Dead cranes were detected accurately in water bodies (AP@50 ≈ 0.90), but detection in terrestrial feeding areas remained more limited (AP@50 ≈ 0.64–0.70), based on aerial annotations without in situ confirmation. Oversampling, undersampling, and focal loss provided limited improvement, suggesting that class imbalance alone does not fully explain the lower terrestrial detection performance, and that carcass scarcity, limited visual diversity, and ambiguity against heterogeneous ground backgrounds may also contribute. Joint multi-habitat training and transfer learning improved generalization for the rare dead-crane class on land. These findings demonstrate the value of UAV-based deep learning for rapid mortality assessment and hotspot identification during wildlife disease outbreaks.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores the use of UAV-based deep learning for rapid detection of Common Crane mortality during an H5N1 avian influenza outbreak in the Hula Valley, Israel. The research highlights the importance of efficient surveillance methods for wildlife disease outbreaks, as traditional field surveys are often slow and labor-intensive. High-resolution RGB imagery was collected from aquatic and terrestrial habitats, and a YOLOv8 detection framework was tested using various training strategies. The results showed reliable detection of living cranes across habitats, with high accuracy in water bodies for dead cranes but limited performance in terrestrial areas. The study suggests that UAV-based deep learning can be a valuable tool for identifying mortality hotspots, though challenges remain in detecting dead cranes on land due to factors like carcass scarcity and visual ambiguity. The evidence indicates moderate confidence in the effectiveness of the method for certain conditions, but limitations in terrestrial detection performance highlight the need for further refinement.

analysis_zh.methods: 高分辨率RGB图像在水生栖息地和陆地觅食栖息地采集,并进行标注以区分存活和死亡个体。基于YOLOv8的检测框架通过特定栖息地训练、多栖息地联合训练和从大型鸟类数据集进行的迁移学习进行了测试,同时结合选择性数据增强、滑动窗口推理和加权框融合技术。
analysis_zh.main_results: 存活的白鹤在不同栖息地中被可靠检测,其在拼接觅食区图像中的AP@50达到0.89,在原始觅食区图像中的AP@50达到0.98。死亡的白鹤在水体中被准确检测(AP@50≈0.90),但在陆地觅食区的检测仍较为有限(AP@50≈0.64–0.70),这是基于空中标注而没有现场确认的结果。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现展示了基于无人机的深度学习在野生动物疾病暴发期间进行快速热点识别和评估的价值。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为禽流感 暴发期间野生动物死亡率快速死亡率工具的开发提供信息,有助于缓解生态风险和人畜共患病风险管理。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 过采样、欠采样和焦点损失提供了有限的改进,表明仅类别不平衡并不能完全解释陆地检测性能较低的原因,而尸体稀缺、视觉多样性有限以及与异质地面背景的模糊性也可能有所贡献。

full_text: Disclaimer: Early release articles are not considered as final versions. Any changes will be reflected in the online version in the month the article is officially released. Volume 32, Number 12—December 2026 Research Letter Serologic Evidence of Avian Influenza Virus Exposure in Livestock, Egypt, 2024–2026 Suggested citation for this article Abstract Spillover of influenza A(H5N1) virus to cattle in the United States sparked global concern. We investigated whether endemic avian influenza viruses are potentially spilling over into domestic livestock in Egypt. We detected influenza H9N2 antibodies in 2.5% and H5N1 antibodies in 2.9%–4.5% of tested animals. Additional surveillance will elucidate host infection dynamics. The emergence of highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) clade 2.3.4.4b virus in dairy cattle in the United States represented a major shift in influenza virus ecology, marking the first sustained transmission of H5N1 virus in a mammalian livestock species (1). Genotype B3.13 was reported in dairy cows in early 2024 in several US states; data indicated a spillover event from wild birds to cattle and then interstate transmission through cow movement (1). A defining feature of H5N1 virus infection in dairy cattle is its marked tropism for the mammary gland, resulting in extremely high viral titers in milk and relatively lower viral loads in respiratory samples (2). Mechanical transmission via the milking process is believed to play a major role in cow-to-cow transmission, particularly in large dairy operations. Cow infection was not limited to genotype B3.13; European genotype euDG was shown to be able to cause infection in an experimental setting (3), and North American genotype D1.1 was detected in cattle in the United States (3). Infection of other livestock species, including goats, sheep, swine, and alpacas, was reported in mixed-species backyards and farms in the United States and United Kingdom (4,5). In 2026, a farm in the Netherlands had a cat infected with H5N1 virus; a cow at that farm had antibodies against the virus (6). Clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 virus and low-pathogenicity avian influenza A(H9N2) virus are widely and endemically circulating in poultry in Egypt on farms and backyards and at live bird markets (7). Subtype H5N1 was detected in feral rats in poultry production areas (8). In addition, reassortment events between the H5N1 and H9N2 subtypes led to the emergence of novel clade 2.3.4.4b influenza A(H5N2) viruses (9). To determine whether those viruses are spilling over to livestock in Egypt, particularly in mixed-species settings, we conducted a serosurveillance study in northern Egypt. During October 2024–January 2026, we collected 444 serum samples from 33 conveniently selected small farms (≈10 cattle, no mixed species) and backyards housing cattle (1–3 cattle with mixed species) in 3 governorates (n = 155, n = 59, and n = 230) in northern Egypt, representing common practices in Egypt. Sheep and goats were also sampled if housed in the same backyards as cattle. All sampled animals were apparently healthy adults. We tested serum samples for antibodies against a 2025 Egyptian clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 (A/duck/Egypt/BA20361C/2022) virus using hemagglutination inhibition (HI) and microneutralization (MN) assays and against a G1-like Egypt influenza A(H9N2) (A/chicken/Egypt/RA20191OP/2022) virus by HI in accordance with World Health Organization protocols (10). We considered an antibody titer >1:40 as positive for both assays. Data on the number of cows, presence of other mammals (e.g., donkeys and horses), and presence of avian species (poultry and/or wild birds) were available for 271 samples. We performed statistical comparisons with χ2 or Fisher exact tests; we considered p<0.05 statistically significant. Overall, 11 (2.5%) serum specimens tested positive for influenza A(H9N2) antibodies, 20 (4.5%) were positive for influenza A(H5N1) antibodies by HI, and 13 (2.9%) were positive for influenza A(H5N1) antibodies by MN (Figure, panel A). Positive titers were 40–160 (Figure, panel B). None of the samples tested positive for antibodies against both viruses. Of the 20 H5N1 virus specimens positive by HI, 12 tested positive by MN; 1 specimen was negative by HI and positive by MN. All influenza H9N2-positive specimens were from 3 locations in the same governorate (p = 0.005). Influenza A(H5N1) antibodies were detected in 2 governorates; the differences in detection rates by governorate were statistically significant (0%, 1.3%, and 4.8%; p = 0.049). All H5N1 virus–seropositive specimens were from cattle (Table). We detected H9N2 antibodies in 6/374 (1.6%) of cattle specimens, 1/31 (3.2%) of goat specimens, and 4/39 (10.3%) of sheep specimens (p = 0.004). Presence of other animals did not predict seropositivity. Small farms had a significantly higher proportion of H5N1 virus–positive animals tested by MN (p = 0.039). Our findings indicate that spillover of avian influenza viruses to cattle and other livestock is not geographically restricted or caused by certain genotypes of H5N1 virus. Clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 virus of the EA-2021-AB genotype and G1-like H9N2 virus appear to be spilling over into livestock in Egypt; however, because our evidence is serologic, we could not ascertain whether true infection is occurring and whether the same signs seen in the United States are common in cattle in Egypt. Even so, the evidence is a strong indicator that spillover is occurring, similar to that reported in Europe (4,6). Furthermore, spillover is not restricted to cattle; some sheep and goats tested in our study were seropositive for influenza A(H9N2) virus. Surveillance for avian influenza viruses in Egypt and other countries, especially those in which avian influenza is endemic, will verify infection and provide data on frequency, routes of transmission, and factors affecting infection of and transmission to livestock. Dr. Gomaa is a virologist at the National Research Centre, Giza, and a member of the Center of Scientific Excellence for virus research. His work focuses on emerging and reemerging viruses, avian influenza, coronaviruses, vaccine development, viral immunology, and pandemic preparedness. Volume 32, Number 12—December 2026 Research Letter Serologic Evidence of Avian Influenza Virus Exposure in Livestock, Egypt, 2024–2026 Suggested citation for this article Abstract Spillover of influenza A(H5N1) virus to cattle in the United States sparked global concern. We investigated whether endemic avian influenza viruses are potentially spilling over into domestic livestock in Egypt. We detected influenza H9N2 antibodies in 2.5% and H5N1 antibodies in 2.9%–4.5% of tested animals. Additional surveillance will elucidate host infection dynamics. The emergence of highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) clade 2.3.4.4b virus in dairy cattle in the United States represented a major shift in influenza virus ecology, marking the first sustained transmission of H5N1 virus in a mammalian livestock species (1). Genotype B3.13 was reported in dairy cows in early 2024 in several US states; data indicated a spillover event from wild birds to cattle and then interstate transmission through cow movement (1). A defining feature of H5N1 virus infection in dairy cattle is its marked tropism for the mammary gland, resulting in extremely high viral titers in milk and relatively lower viral loads in respiratory samples (2). Mechanical transmission via the milking process is believed to play a major role in cow-to-cow transmission, particularly in large dairy operations. Cow infection was not limited to genotype B3.13; European genotype euDG was shown to be able to cause infection in an experimental setting (3), and North American genotype D1.1 was detected in cattle in the United States (3). Infection of other livestock species, including goats, sheep, swine, and alpacas, was reported in mixed-species backyards and farms in the United States and United Kingdom (4,5). In 2026, a farm in the Netherlands had a cat infected with H5N1 virus; a cow at that farm had antibodies against the virus (6). Clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 virus and low-pathogenicity avian influenza A(H9N2) virus are widely and endemically circulating in poultry in Egypt on farms and backyards and at live bird markets (7). Subtype H5N1 was detected in feral rats in poultry production areas (8). In addition, reassortment events between the H5N1 and H9N2 subtypes led to the emergence of novel clade 2.3.4.4b influenza A(H5N2) viruses (9). To determine whether those viruses are spilling over to livestock in Egypt, particularly in mixed-species settings, we conducted a serosurveillance study in northern Egypt. During October 2024–January 2026, we collected 444 serum samples from 33 conveniently selected small farms (≈10 cattle, no mixed species) and backyards housing cattle (1–3 cattle with mixed species) in 3 governorates (n = 155, n = 59, and n = 230) in northern Egypt, representing common practices in Egypt. Sheep and goats were also sampled if housed in the same backyards as cattle. All sampled animals were apparently healthy adults. We tested serum samples for antibodies against a 2025 Egyptian clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 (A/duck/Egypt/BA20361C/2022) virus using hemagglutination inhibition (HI) and microneutralization (MN) assays and against a G1-like Egypt influenza A(H9N2) (A/chicken/Egypt/RA20191OP/2022) virus by HI in accordance with World Health Organization protocols (10). We considered an antibody titer >1:40 as positive for both assays. Data on the number of cows, presence of other mammals (e.g., donkeys and horses), and presence of avian species (poultry and/or wild birds) were available for 271 samples. We performed statistical comparisons with χ2 or Fisher exact tests; we considered p<0.05 statistically significant. Overall, 11 (2.5%) serum specimens tested positive for influenza A(H9N2) antibodies, 20 (4.5%) were positive for influenza A(H5N1) antibodies by HI, and 13 (2.9%) were positive for influenza A(H5N1) antibodies by MN (Figure, panel A). Positive titers were 40–160 (Figure, panel B). None of the samples tested positive for antibodies against both viruses. Of the 20 H5N1 virus specimens positive by HI, 12 tested positive by MN; 1 specimen was negative by HI and positive by MN. All influenza H9N2-positive specimens were from 3 locations in the same governorate (p = 0.005). Influenza A(H5N1) antibodies were detected in 2 governorates; the differences in detection rates by governorate were statistically significant (0%, 1.3%, and 4.8%; p = 0.049). All H5N1 virus–seropositive specimens were from cattle (Table). We detected H9N2 antibodies in 6/374 (1.6%) of cattle specimens, 1/31 (3.2%) of goat specimens, and 4/39 (10.3%) of sheep specimens (p = 0.004). Presence of other animals did not predict seropositivity. Small farms had a significantly higher proportion of H5N1 virus–positive animals tested by MN (p = 0.039). Our findings indicate that spillover of avian influenza viruses to cattle and other livestock is not geographically restricted or caused by certain genotypes of H5N1 virus. Clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 virus of the EA-2021-AB genotype and G1-like H9N2 virus appear to be spilling over into livestock in Egypt; however, because our evidence is serologic, we could not ascertain whether true infection is occurring and whether the same signs seen in the United States are common in cattle in Egypt. Even so, the evidence is a strong indicator that spillover is occurring, similar to that reported in Europe (4,6). Furthermore, spillover is not restricted to cattle; some sheep and goats tested in our study were seropositive for influenza A(H9N2) virus. Surveillance for avian influenza viruses in Egypt and other countries, especially those in which avian influenza is endemic, will verify infection and provide data on frequency, routes of transmission, and factors affecting infection of and transmission to livestock. Dr. Gomaa is a virologist at the National Research Centre, Giza, and a member of the Center of Scientific Excellence for virus research. His work focuses on emerging and reemerging viruses, avian influenza, coronaviruses, vaccine development, viral immunology, and pandemic preparedness.
